# Divergences between the Rust twin (skia_rust_unicode::icu_shim on ICU4X =2.3.0 stock compiled data for breaks,
# properties, case and locales; unicode-bidi =0.3.18 for bidi) and Chromium ICU 78.2 (d578f2e8):
# `<key> <class>[+<class>...]`. Every other row, range and conformance line is exact.
# A listed entry that starts matching, or a divergence that is not listed, fails the replay test.
# Generated by classify.py (docs/design/modules.md §3.4). Keys: `<case> <source> <index>` for a string,
# `prop|cp <name> <first>-<last> <icu>/<icu4x>` for a range of code points, `conf <file> <line> icu-only|icu4x-only`
# for a conformance-test line that only one engine fails, `misc <call>` for a misc line.
#
# The shim of M2 emulates what ICU4X does not report: rule status (word, line, sentence, including the status of
# dictionary boundaries), ubrk_following/ubrk_preceding at offsets inside a code point, ICU's numbering of
# properties, u_strToUpper's locales, uloc_forLanguageTag. The classes word-status-*, line-status-*,
# sentence-status-sep and nav-offset-inside-code-point of M0c are gone; what is left is break data (M4) and
# bidi (M3). Classes:
#
# Word breaks (UAX #29)
#   word-dot                    Chromium's wordbrk.patch moves `.` and U+FF0E from MidNumLet to MidNum, so ICU
#                               breaks around them in places ICU4X (stock UAX #29) does not (`SkCanvas.h`).
#   word-colon                  the same patch removes `:` from MidLetter: ICU breaks `a:b`, ICU4X does not.
#   word-hangul-syllable-jamo   ICU breaks a precomposed Hangul syllable from a following conjoining jamo
#                               (U+AC00 U+11A8), which UAX #29 (and ICU4X) keep in one word.
#   word-dictionary-cj          boundaries next to Han, Hiragana or Katakana that differ: ICU's cjdict (with
#                               cjdict.patch) against ICU4X's dictionary.
#   word-dictionary-sa          boundaries next to Thai, Lao, Khmer, Myanmar, Tai Tham or New Tai Lue characters:
#                               ICU's dictionaries (lstm.patch, khmer-dictbe.patch, laodict.txt) against ICU4X's models.
# Line breaks (UAX #14)
#   line-dictionary-sa          Thai/Lao/Khmer/Myanmar/Tai Tham/New Tai Lue breaks: dictionary vs LSTM.
#   line-normal-other           a break ICU makes after U+FE13 (`a\ufe13b`) that ICU4X's Normal strictness does not.
# Navigation (ubrk_following / ubrk_preceding): a function of the boundaries; a nav row takes the classes of the
# boundaries of its line-u8 or word-u16 row.
# Bidi (UAX #9)
#   bidi-direction              ubidi_getDirection is directionFromFlags (ubidi.cpp#L1007-L1020): it follows which strong
#                               types occur in the text (LTR when there is no R, AL, RLE, RLO or RLI), adjusted for the
#                               paragraph level (MIXED for RTL text in an LTR paragraph), not the resolved levels the
#                               twin derives it from.
#   bidi-uniform-direction-shortcut  when directionFromFlags is LTR or RTL, ICU does not resolve the text: every level
#                               is the paragraph level, whatever explicit embeddings, overrides or isolates the text
#                               contains; unicode-bidi applies them (U+202D abc: ICU 0 0 0 0, unicode-bidi 0 2 2 2).
#   bidi-x9-removed-levels      the level of characters rule X9 removes (LRE, RLE, LRO, RLO, PDF, BN): ICU gives an
#                               opening character the level it opens and a closing one the outer level;
#                               unicode-bidi gives them the previous character's level.
#   bidi-isolate-levels         levels of isolate initiators and PDI.
#   bidi-default-level-number-after-separator  UBIDI_DEFAULT_RTL: a number after an empty paragraph (`\n\n2 abc`)
#                               gets level 2 in ICU (as if the last strong direction were R), 0 in unicode-bidi (W7).
#   bidi-levels-other           any other level difference.
# Conformance files
#   icu-bidi-conformance        BidiCharacterTest.txt lines that ICU fails and the twin passes.
#   icu4x-lb-<rule>             LineBreakTest.txt lines that ICU passes and ICU4X (Normal strictness, compiled data)
#                               fails; <rule> is the UAX #14 rule the file names at the first wrong slot (20.1:
#                               HH, 9.0: combining marks after SA/unassigned/East Asian characters, 28.0, 999.0,
#                               ...). Not root-caused further: both engines fail the 142 lines in which Chromium's
#                               line_normal.patch departs from the file, so those are not divergences.
#   word-colon                  WordBreakTest.txt lines (rule 6.0, `a:a`) ICU fails and ICU4X passes.
bidi-auto-ltr synthetic 100 bidi-direction+bidi-uniform-direction-shortcut

bidi-auto-ltr synthetic 102 bidi-direction+bidi-uniform-direction-shortcut
